correctness.rationale: For every nonempty eligible update batch S, each internal moved edge contributes at most one successor-neighbor count because kappa>=3; boundary successor edges P then satisfy P>=sum theta-|I|. Exactly P boundary edges become monochromatic and Q equal-color boundary edges cease to be, so delta Phi=P-Q>=2P-|B|>=sum_S(2theta_v-degree_v). Finite edge budget implies the claimed global update and round bounds. Tripartite three-cycles and bipartite two-color cycles show the two excluded boundaries. Exact finite tests on the embedded verifier passed 1,319,754 full trajectories and 5,001 partial update checks, plus other tests; the proof, not enumeration, establishes all finite sizes.

value.rationale: The 2026 source motivates high-threshold cyclic-dominance fixation, and the theorem supplies an all-configurations structural global stabilization criterion with a linear edge-budget, heterogeneous thresholds and arbitrary synchronous eligible batches. It identifies a necessary universal sharp boundary via a nontrivial three-color periodic family and a structurally different binary case. This is not a textbook majority conclusion: binary synchronous majority updates can oscillate, while the cyclic successor constraint forbids reciprocal edge contributions.
